To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

p38 is activated in vHMeC, which express high levels of COX- 2, and that COX-2 is expressed in the nuclei of epithelial cells in premalignant lesions and in morphologically normal tissue in the vicinity of these lesions.
p38 kinase is a key upstream regulator of COX- 2 and is activated in vHIMEC as well as in human breast tissue.
p38 is activated in premaligant mammary tissue and is responsible for COX-2 regulation in vHMECs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
identifying the mechanisms that regulate the expression of CO2 in normal and malignant breast tissue and the role of this enzyme in breast tumorigenesis.
the regulation of CO2 expression in human mammary cells, and the role of COX-1 and COX-2 as mediators of breast carcinogenesis.
the role that p38 MAP kinase and its downstream target, cyclooxygen-ase-2, play in breast tumorigenesis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
COX-2 overexpression in breast epithelial cells is regulated by p38 and is associated with breast carcinogenesis.
COX-2 is a downstream target of p38 in the vHMEC model system.

p38 is activated in premaligant tissue, and this may be an upstream pathway to COX-2 induction.

The main takeaway from our work is that
p38 is a novel regulator of COX- 2 and is activated in breast cancer.
